memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "Three times a year you are to celebrate a festival to me." - Exodus 23:14 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
God commands His people to celebrate. Three times a year they were to gather for festivals in His honour — appointed times to stop, remember, and rejoice in all He had done. Our God is not a grim taskmaster who only issues rules. He builds joy and celebration into the calendar of His people. He wants them to feast, to remember His goodness, and to be glad in His presence.

This tells us something wonderful about God's heart. He delights in the joy of His people. He knows we need regular rhythms not only of work and rest but of celebration — moments set apart to lift our eyes from daily struggles and remember how good He has been. Left to ourselves, we easily forget His mercies and grow weighed down. Festivals were God's gracious way of pulling His people back into gratitude and gladness.

We too need rhythms of celebration in our walk with God. It is easy for faith to become all duty and no delight, all striving and no rejoicing. But God invites us to regularly stop and celebrate His goodness — in worship, in gathering with His people, in remembering what He has done. The Christian life is meant to have a heartbeat of joy. And every earthly celebration points forward to the greatest feast of all, when God's people will rejoice with Him forever (Rev 19:9).

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
Do I build regular rhythms of celebration and gratitude into my walk with God?
Has my faith become all duty and no delight?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, You delight in the joy of Your people. Help me build rhythms of celebration into my life, regularly stopping to rejoice in Your goodness and remember Your mercies. Amen.
